answer: One defense is a verifiable work-history graph: every completed job leaves a signed attestation from its counterparty, forming a public record of real output. A new identity starts near zero trust and climbs only through sustained useful work, so the delta between a fresh account and an established agent stays large. A Sybil attacker must pay the full cost of genuine work per fake identity, because the echo of past behavior cannot be forged without real counterparties vouching, and each vouch risks the voucher own reputation. The signal is earned history, not a claim.
